findings.title: `die` echoes its own exit-code argument into the message
findings.description: The new helper `die() { echo "error: $*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }` prints the whole argument list, so every call that passes an exit code as the second argument renders the code as part of the message. In `b2_lifecycle.sh` the four call sites are `die "unknown argument: $1" 2`, `die "${pair%%:*} is required" 2`, `die "at least one prefix is required" 2`, and `die "--days must be a whole number: $DAYS" 2`; each produces `error: unknown argument: -x 2`, `error: --days must be a whole number: abc 2`, etc. The exit code is correct, but the operator-facing message is wrong. The pattern is copied from `deploy/lib/render_cron.sh` (pre-existing), so the new file inherits it; the fix is `echo "error: $1"` so the message stays the first argument.

findings.title: `render_cron.sh` prints the exit code in the `--pgdata` error
findings.description: The new `die "no --pgdata for cluster $name" 2` call goes through the same `die` helper, so `render_cron.sh --pgdata ...` prints `error: no --pgdata for cluster 17/tick 2`. The test `test_missing_pgdata_for_a_row_refused` only asserts the substring `no --pgdata for cluster 17/tick`, so it does not catch the trailing `2`. The fix is the same as above: `die` should echo `$1` only.

findings.title: `grep -v` on a comment-only template exits under `set -e`
findings.description: `CLUSTER_TEXT=$(grep -v '^##' "$CLUSTER_TEMPLATE")` runs under `set -euo pipefail`. `grep -v` exits 1 when it produces no output, so a template that contains only `##` lines (or an empty file) terminates the render with a bare non-zero exit instead of a diagnostic. The current template has nine lines, so this is not hit today, but a template edit that removes the last job line would fail with no explanation. Adding `|| true` or a `[ -s ... ]` check keeps the error message.
